content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm currently using [product_name] for activating school bells at scheduled times. The device operates independently without any internet access. After three months, I've noticed the device’s real-time clock has drifted by over 1 minute and 30 seconds. To fix this, I have to visit the site to manually adjust the time. Why is such a significant time drift occurring in such a short period? Is there a technical reason for this? Most electronic watches don't experience this level of inaccuracy. Is there a way to resolve or reduce this issue? Thank you for any help.

According to the manual: Typical real-time clock accuracy is ±2 seconds per day. This means a time difference of around 3 minutes after three months is within normal specifications. For improved accuracy, synchronization with an NTP server is recommended.
I agree—it's surprising! Thank you for the clarification.
If your network has a NTP server, you can synchronize the device’s date and time for much better accuracy. Hope this information is useful.

analysis.insight_summary: Users observed notable time drift (over 1 minute, 30 seconds in three months) in a standalone [product_name] device’s real-time clock. The documented clock accuracy specifications explain the drift, yet users are surprised compared to common electronic watches, indicating an expectation gap regarding performance.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] device’s internal real-time clock to maintain high accuracy over several months, similar to standard electronic watches, so manual interventions or site visits are minimized.
